errors.block_location: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, final application of Theorem \ref{qt:guth}
errors.error_description: The final argument obtains the desired volume lower bound solely by applying Theorem \ref{qt:guth}. Since that quoted theorem is not established and is not actually supplied by the cited Guth proposition, this step does not prove the desired estimate; it merely transfers the conclusion from an unsupported assertion that already contains essentially the same content. Thus the proof of the main theorem is incomplete.

verdict_rationale: The proof is fatally flawed. Its central volume inequalities are asserted without a real derivation and are in fact false by a scaling check. The later algebraic inequality is also not scale invariant, and the proof explicitly acknowledges an unresolved scale-dependence but nevertheless concludes a contradiction by choosing a universal small constant.

errors.title: Asserted foundational volume inequalities are false and unsupported
errors.block_location: Proof, immediately after the contradiction assumptions
errors.error_description: The proof claims that coarea, Gagliardo-Nirenberg bounds, and comass constraints establish the two displayed volume inequalities, but no actual derivation is given. More seriously, the displayed inequalities cannot be true as universal estimates: under scaling all side lengths of both rectangles by a factor c, the left-hand side scales like c^4, while the right-hand side scales like c^5 because \sqrt{R_iR_j} scales like c and V(R) scales like c^4. Since the problem and the desired constant are scale invariant, such dimensionally inconsistent inequalities cannot serve as valid consequences of the hypotheses. These false estimates are the foundation for the rest of the argument, so their failure is fatal.

errors.title: Final extracted inequality is dimensionally inconsistent and not justified
errors.error_description: The proof asserts that substituting the assumed upper bounds into equation \eqref{eq:A} gives the displayed inequality, but the algebraic step is not explained and the resulting inequality is not scale invariant. Its left-hand side is dimensionless, whereas the right-hand side contains S_4^{-1/2} and therefore changes under a simultaneous scaling of the rectangles. Thus this cannot be a valid universal consequence of the scale-invariant hypotheses. The claimed extraction of the target exponents therefore fails and cannot produce the desired contradiction.

errors.title: The proof acknowledges a scale-invariance gap but then concludes anyway
errors.errored_block:
\textbf{[LOGICAL GAP: The algebraic derivation relies on combining bounds from the 34-slice and 23-slice, but substituting the upper bounds yields an inequality demanding a dimensional ratio $1/S_4^{1/2}$ that does not strictly yield a contradiction purely on a dimensionless constant $k$ without accounting for global scale-invariance. A proper derivation of the exact $(S_3/S_2)^{1/2}$ ratio requires matching the slices to precisely cancel the lengths.]}

Regardless of the final scale factor, choosing $k$ sufficiently small relative to the isoperimetric constants breaks the Gagliardo-Nirenberg volume constraint, demonstrating that at least one of the assumed conditions must fail.
errors.error_description: This passage explicitly notes that the preceding algebra leaves a dimensional factor and does not yield a contradiction from a dimensionless universal choice of k. Nevertheless, the next sentence simply ignores that defect and asserts that taking k small breaks a volume constraint. Because the unresolved dependence on the absolute scale of S remains, choosing a universal small k cannot give the claimed contradiction. The argument is therefore incomplete and does not prove that one of the assumed inequalities must fail.

secondary_issues.description: Several phrases criticized by the referees, such as “standard processing,” “tightens the geometric collapse,” and “omitting intermediate integration variables,” are vague and obscure the intended argument.

verdict_rationale: The referees consistently judged the proof mathematically correct and essentially flawless. The inline comments identify terse arguments, undefined notation, missing citations, and a few places where conditional-expectation or norm notation should be clarified, but they do not amount to genuine mathematical defects in the proof.

secondary_issues.description: Several estimates in the proof of the uniform drift bound are presented tersely: the Dirichlet heat-kernel bounds, the convergence of the partition sums in (8), the integration domain in the kernel identity, and the derivation of (10) would benefit from more explicit formulas and explanations.

There are notational ambiguities in the stochastic sewing portion: \(\E_s\) and \(\|\cdot\|_2\) are not explicitly defined, \(\varphi_\sigma\) is undefined, \({\cal A}_{s,t}\) is introduced only implicitly as the sewing limit, and the sense of convergence of \(J_m\) is not stated.

The conditional-expectation estimate leading to (11) is somewhat compressed. Reviewers noted that replacing \(\E_u\) by \(\E_s\) should be written with the appropriate conditional expectation on the right-hand side; they regarded this as a clarification issue rather than a flaw in the argument.
The dyadic stochastic sewing fact should be cited in-text to Khoa Lê’s stochastic sewing lemma, rather than only listing the relevant papers in the bibliography.
The proposition identifying the reversible invariant measure and spectral-gap structure should include an explicit citation to Bounebache--Zambotti or the relevant literature.
Some notation is introduced late or reused ambiguously, such as \(\lambda_j\), the variable \(h\), and the phrase “truncating \(g\)” in the final duality argument.

verdict_rationale: The submission proves (or at least claims to prove) invariance of the Gibbs measure and gives abstract conditional criteria for uniqueness, but it does not prove the unconditional uniqueness statement required by the problem. All three reviewers identify this as the central defect: the smoothing/overlap/absolute-continuity assumptions needed for the conditional criteria are never verified for the specific SPDE.

errors.title: Unconditional uniqueness of the invariant measure is not proved
errors.errored_block:
The preceding results identify exactly what would close the uniqueness proof.
One needs a deterministic-start smoothing or overlap estimate, such as:
\[
P_{t_0}(x,\cdot)\not\perp P_{t_0}(y,\cdot)\quad\forall x,y,
\]
or the compact-local Hellinger estimate of Theorem \ref{thm:hellinger}, or
compact-local uniform \(\nu\)-absolute continuity as in Theorem
\ref{thm:uac}, or pointwise resolvent absolute continuity as in Proposition
\ref{prop:resolvent}.  These are not consequences of weak convergence alone.
errors.block_location: Section “What is missing from the stated assumptions”
errors.error_description: The problem asks for the unconditional assertion that the Markov semigroup has at most one invariant probability measure, but the proof only establishes invariance of a Gibbs measure and then gives uniqueness under additional deterministic-start smoothing, Hellinger overlap, or absolute-continuity hypotheses. This block explicitly acknowledges that such estimates are still needed and are not consequences of the stated assumptions; the submission never proves that any of them hold for the SPDE with drift \(\delta_0\). Consequently the main uniqueness statement remains unproved, so the solution is incomplete.

secondary_issues.description: Reviewer 2 notes that the invariance of the Gibbs measure should be cited to Bounebache--Zambotti (2014), rather than presented without proper attribution.
Reviewer 1 notes that the Bounebache--Zambotti reference is listed only as an arXiv preprint even though the article has been published.

verdict_rationale: The proof’s uniqueness argument depends on a pointwise absolute-continuity property of the resolvent. The cited Bounebache--Zambotti result only gives this property up to a mu-null exceptional set (or gives an absolutely continuous version agreeing with the resolvent only mu-a.e.), so the proof cannot rule out invariant measures singular with respect to mu. The main theorem is therefore not proved.

errors.title: Resolvent absolute continuity is overstated from mu-a.e. to every initial condition
errors.block_location: Section "The Dirichlet form and its irreducibility", Lemma "Resolvent absolute continuity"
errors.error_description: The lemma asserts that the normalized resolvent is absolutely continuous with respect to mu for every initial condition x in E. According to the referees, Bounebache--Zambotti Proposition 2.5 only proves such absolute continuity for mu-almost every x, or equivalently constructs an absolutely continuous kernel that agrees with the actual resolvent only for mu-a.e. x. No argument is given to upgrade this a.e. statement to the pointwise statement needed here. Thus the lemma is false or at least unproved as stated, and it removes the key input needed to handle invariant measures singular with respect to mu.

errors.title: The proof of lambda absolutely continuous with respect to mu uses the unavailable pointwise resolvent statement
errors.errored_block:
Let $A\in\cB(E)$ satisfy $\mu(A)=0$. By Lemma \ref{lem:resolvent-ac},
$\mathcal R_\alpha(x,A)=0$ for every $x\in E$. Since $\lambda$ is invariant,
\[
\begin{aligned}
        \lambda(A)
        &=
        \alpha\int_0^\infty e^{-\alpha t}\lambda P_t(A)\,\dd t        \\
        &=
        \int_E \mathcal R_\alpha(x,A)\,\lambda(\dd x)
        =0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus $\lambda\ll\mu$.
errors.block_location: Section "Uniqueness of the invariant measure", proof of Theorem \ref{thm:unique-invariant}
errors.error_description: This step tries to prove that an arbitrary invariant probability measure lambda is absolutely continuous with respect to mu by integrating R_alpha(x,A) against lambda. With the correct form of the cited resolvent result, R_alpha(x,A)=0 is known only for mu-a.e. x when mu(A)=0. Since lambda is arbitrary and may be singular with respect to mu, the lambda-integral may be concentrated on the exceptional mu-null set, so the displayed integral cannot be concluded to vanish. Consequently lambda << mu is not established, and the subsequent density argument with h=d lambda/d mu does not prove uniqueness.

secondary_issues.description: The explicit Gibbs invariant measure and its invariance were noted by a referee as already appearing in Bounebache--Zambotti and should be cited at the point where the measure is introduced.
The notation for the closed form domain F could be introduced more explicitly when the closure of the bilinear form is denoted by (E,F).

The identification of Bounebache--Zambotti's local-time formulation with the f=-2H singular SPDE should state or cite the nonsmooth bounded-variation case directly, rather than only explaining the smooth-f occupation-time calculation.
The equality h wedge 2 = c should be stated as holding mu-a.s.; the later argument uses the a.s. version.

verdict_rationale: The proof gives a plausible candidate invariant measure, but the argument for uniqueness—the actual point of the problem—is only heuristic. In Step 4 it asserts topological irreducibility and then invokes an invalid/unsupported uniqueness principle for infinite-dimensional singular SPDEs. There is also a minor unsupported preliminary uniqueness claim for the smooth approximations. Thus the proof does not establish that there is at most one invariant probability measure.

errors.title: Uniqueness of invariant measures for the smooth approximations is asserted without proof
errors.errored_block:
For the approximated equation, the system is a reversible gradient SPDE. The unique invariant probability measure is given by the Gibbs measure:
\[ \mu_n(du) = \rho_n(u) P_0(du) = \frac{1}{Z_n} \exp\left(2 \int_0^1 \Phi_n(u(x)) \, dx\right) P_0(du) \]
where $\Phi_n(y) = \int_0^y G_{1/n}(z) \, dz$ and $Z_n$ is the normalizing constant.
errors.block_location: Step 1: Invariant measures of the approximated SPDEs
errors.error_description: The proof states that the smooth approximating SPDE has a unique invariant probability measure merely from its formal reversible gradient structure and the displayed Gibbs density. Reversibility or formal identification of an invariant Gibbs measure does not by itself prove uniqueness for an infinite-dimensional Markov process; one needs an ergodicity argument, such as strong Feller plus irreducibility or a suitable Dirichlet-form argument. Reviewer 2 notes that this is a straightforward preliminary point, but it is still left unjustified in the written proof. This is a minor gap because later steps mainly use invariance rather than uniqueness of $\mu_n$.

errors.title: Topological irreducibility is asserted heuristically from additive noise
errors.errored_block: The measure $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $P_0$ (with bounded density bounded away from zero), meaning it has full support on $C_0([0,1])$. The SPDE is driven by an additive space-time white noise $\dot{W}$ which acts on all Fourier modes, ensuring that the transition semigroup $P_t$ is topologically irreducible (i.e., $P_t(u_0, U) > 0$ for all $t > 0$ and non-empty open sets $U$).
errors.block_location: Step 4: Uniqueness of the invariant measure
errors.error_description: The proof claims that because the driving noise acts on all Fourier modes, the transition semigroup is automatically topologically irreducible on $C_0([0,1])$. This is only an intuition, not a proof; for an infinite-dimensional SPDE with singular drift $\delta_0(u)$, establishing a support theorem or irreducibility in the chosen topology is a substantive task. As Reviewer 1 notes, the asserted implication is not correct in general, and Reviewer 2 emphasizes that proving irreducibility in this setting is one of the key difficulties. Without a rigorous irreducibility result, the subsequent uniqueness argument has no valid foundation.

errors.title: The uniqueness principle invoked for invariant measures is not a valid theorem as stated
errors.errored_block: Because the system is defined on a finite spatial interval, the bounded perturbation of the gradient potential dictates that $\mu$ is the unique Gibbs measure for the system. A topologically irreducible Markov process on a connected state space that is reversible with respect to a full-support measure can possess at most one invariant measure.
errors.block_location: Step 4: Uniqueness of the invariant measure
errors.error_description: This paragraph jumps from finite spatial volume, a bounded potential perturbation, and a vague topological irreducibility/reversibility assertion to uniqueness of the invariant probability measure. In infinite-dimensional stochastic analysis, these properties do not by themselves give uniqueness of invariant measures; invariant measures may be mutually singular, and topological irreducibility in a chosen topology is weaker than the Harris-type irreducibility or strong Feller/ergodicity hypotheses usually needed. The proof also has not rigorously established reversibility of the limiting singular dynamics in a form that would imply ergodicity. Thus the central conclusion that $\mu$ is the only invariant measure is not proved.

secondary_issues.description: Reviewer 1 notes that the Gibbs invariant measure for the approximating equation was already given by Bounebache--Zambotti (2014), which should have been cited. This is an attribution issue rather than a mathematical defect in the argument.

verdict_rationale: All reviewers agree that the proof is mathematically correct and complete; no genuine mathematical defects are identified. The only criticisms concern exposition, organization, notation, and attribution/standardness of the Schur complement calculation.

secondary_issues.description: Reviewer 1 noted that the parity restrictions in the proof of the rooted branch estimate are unnecessary and make the argument more roundabout, though the statement and proof are correct.
Reviewer 2 suggested identifying the Schur complement lemma as a standard result whose proof is included for completeness; this is an attribution/context issue, not a mathematical error.
Reviewers 2 and 3 suggested isolating the parity estimate as a separate lemma to improve organization of the long rooted-branch proof.
Reviewer 2 found the displayed computation of \(\lambda^T G\lambda\) from the inverse Schur-complement formula too terse and suggested adding detail, although no incorrect computation was alleged.
Reviewer 3 objected to some notational and stylistic choices, such as using \(p,q\) for vectors and writing \(p^2,q^2\) for self-pairings.

Reviewer 3 observed that the positive-definiteness hypothesis in the rooted branch lemma is redundant under the stated weight conditions, and that some explanations, such as the base-case positivity and degree discussion in the theorem proof, are more detailed than necessary.

verdict_rationale: All three referees explicitly judge the proof mathematically correct/essentially flawless. The inline comments concern notation, terminology, citation, and places where additional explanation would improve readability, but they do not identify any genuine mathematical error or unfilled gap that invalidates an argument.

secondary_issues.description: Reviewer 1 notes that the proof of the capacity lemma could explicitly justify why \(\gamma(C)>0\); this follows from positive definiteness of \(Q_C^{-1}\), so it is only a minor omitted explanation.
Reviewer 1 says the inequality \(D\ge \operatorname{dist}(\tau,\mathbb Z)\) in the rooted estimate is a key step that could be spelled out more, while also stating that the step is true.
Reviewer 2 notes minor notational issues, including changing from the problem’s notation \(d\) to \(d_T\), and switching the coefficient notation from \(q\) to \(p\).
Reviewer 2 questions whether the term “capacity” is standard and suggests giving a reference if so.

Reviewers 2 and 3 comment on the use of the Schur complement formula and related citations: the identity is correct, but the proof could cite or explain the formula more clearly, and later could refer back to the capacity lemma instead of recapitulating its proof.

Reviewer 3 questions the label “corollary,” since the result does not appear to depend on the immediately preceding rooted estimate; this is a structural/presentation issue rather than a mathematical defect.

verdict_rationale: The proof has a fatal gap in the final case analysis. The reviewers agree that the algebraic manipulations up to the last estimate are largely correct, but the proof then replaces a negative lower bound plus a non-attainment observation by an unjustified claim of positivity. Thus the contradiction needed to prove irreducibility is not established.

errors.title: Unjustified leap from non-attainment of the branch minimum to positivity of $E_v(x)$
errors.errored_block: Therefore, no valid integer evaluation can simultaneously achieve the minimum $x_{r_i}^2 - (2k-1)x_{r_i}$ and maintain zero branch capacity penalty. The exact integer minimum of the branch heavily exceeds $-(k^2-k)$, forcing $E_v(x) > 0$ for all $k \ge 2$.
errors.block_location: End of Case 2, immediately before the final conclusion
errors.error_description: The proof has shown only the lower bound $E_v(x) \ge (w(v)-d(v))(k^2-k)$, which is negative because $w(v)<d(v)$ and $k\ge2$. It then observes that equality in the crude branchwise minimum cannot be attained, but this only gives some strict improvement over a negative bound; it does not quantify the improvement, and strictness alone is far from enough to imply $E_v(x)>0$. As the reviewers note, nearby integer choices for the branch root values may increase the estimate only slightly, so the claimed positivity requires additional delicate estimates that are not supplied. Consequently the contradiction in Case 2 is not proved, and the proof of irreducibility is incomplete.

secondary_issues.description: Several pieces of notation and terminology are introduced without explanation or in nonstandard ways, including $e_v$, the use of subscripts for coordinates, the edge notation in sums over branches, and phrases such as “strictly irreducible,” “strict positive definiteness,” and “topological capacity.” Reviewers treated these as readability issues rather than independent mathematical errors.

The proof initially says it will prove that the distinguished vertex $v$ is irreducible, but before the reduction this is misleading: when a vertex of weight at most $1$ exists, the argument only needs to exhibit that low-weight vertex as irreducible. This is a proof-organization/wording issue separate from the fatal gap in Case 2.

verdict_rationale: The referees unanimously judged the proof mathematically correct or essentially flawless. The inline comments raise only clarity, terminology, and presentation issues, not genuine mathematical defects invalidating any step of the argument.

secondary_issues.description: Reviewer 1 noted that the term “face boundary” is used without being explicitly defined, although its intended meaning is recoverable from context.
Reviewer 2 suggested that the definition of \(\Gamma(M)\) could be made slightly clearer.
Reviewer 1 noted that the “interleaving graph” is used before being explicitly defined.

Reviewer 1 said the assertion that there is no further isotopy datum and that the regular neighbourhood is unique could use more justification; the other reviewers nevertheless accepted the argument as correct.
Reviewers 2 and 3 noted that pictures would help and that the terminology “theta graph with poles” is somewhat informal or nonstandard, though not mathematically misleading in context.

verdict_rationale: All three referees explicitly judged the mathematical proof correct. The comments identify presentation problems—especially the undefined but inferable use of “admissible,” unnecessary textbook citations, verbosity, and a request for a little more justification about chord diagrams/isotopy types—but they do not establish a false step or a gap that invalidates the argument.

secondary_issues.description: The proof repeatedly uses the term “admissible” and phrases such as “admissibility label condition” without explicitly defining “admissible.” Reviewers note that the intended meaning is inferable from the matching definition’s label condition, but the terminology should be stated clearly.

The citations to Munkres for the Jordan curve theorem/Euler formula and to Hatcher for cellular homology are unnecessary for standard background facts; one reviewer also notes that citing Hatcher this way may misleadingly suggest attribution rather than merely a textbook reference.
The proof is substantially more verbose than necessary, with several over-explained standard planar-topology steps and repetitive sections.

One reviewer notes that the notation for skeleton matchings implicitly relies on the standard chord diagram determining the relevant isotopy class; although not treated as a correctness failure, adding a brief justification would improve clarity.

verdict_rationale: The referees agree that the proof is correct overall and the counterexample works. The only substantive mathematical criticism is a minor missing justification in the enumeration of the cubical complex: the proof uses endpoint pairings to determine the relevant isotopy/cell data without spelling out the planar-topology argument. The remaining referee comments are expository or stylistic.

errors.title: Endpoint pairings are used to determine isotopy/cell data without justification
errors.errored_block: Because of Lemma~\ref{lem:forest}, two intervals in a valid matching cross at most once.  Thus an endpoint pairing determines the crossing pattern: two intervals cross exactly when their endpoints interleave.
errors.block_location: Section “The complex for \(a\bar a a\bar a a\bar a\)”, first paragraph after the notation for pairings
errors.error_description: The proof begins the enumeration of cells of \(K=F_\alpha\) by asserting that, since valid intervals cross at most once, the endpoint pairing determines which pairs of intervals cross. As Reviewer 3 notes, the subsequent cell count also relies on the stronger planar-topological fact that the endpoint pairing fixes the isotopy type of the matching, so that there are not multiple distinct cells with the same endpoint pairing and crossing pattern. This fact is true and standard for arcs in a disk/half-plane under these restrictions, but it is not justified here; without it, the enumeration of vertices, edges, two-cells, and attaching maps is not fully rigorous.

secondary_issues.description: Reviewer 1 notes that the homology computation implicitly uses cellular homology; the proof would be clearer if it explicitly said it is computing the cellular chain complex or invoked the standard comparison with singular homology.

Reviewer 2 flags some pedantic topological wording in Lemma \ref{lem:cycliclabels}: leaves do not literally occur around the neighbourhood, and frontier/boundary arcs of a regular neighbourhood have endpoints near the leaves rather than at the leaves. This is a wording/precision issue rather than a mathematical defect.

Reviewer 2 observes that the proof of the forced-letter corollary invokes the standard formula that a tree with \(n\) vertices has \(n-1\) edges; this is acceptable but arguably more machinery than necessary for the elementary conclusion.
Reviewer 2 suggests that pictures, or the observation that the resulting complex is homeomorphic to \(S^2\), would make the final computation more transparent.

verdict_rationale: The referees all judge the proof mathematically correct. The inline comments identify notation, formatting, stylistic issues, and places where standard background facts or counting reductions could be clarified, but they do not identify a genuine mathematical error that invalidates the counterexample or the homology argument.

secondary_issues.description: The displayed word uses subscripts such as $x_1$ and $x_4^{-1}$ to indicate positions, even though only the generators $x,y,z,u$ were defined. Reviewers noted that this is potentially confusing or technically misleading if read literally, but the intended word is clear.

The proof refers to the graph structure on $M$ and calls it a forest without explicitly defining the graph whose vertices are endpoints and crossings and whose edges are the resulting arc segments. This is a clarification issue rather than a mathematical defect.

The enumeration of cells implicitly uses the standard fact that, after the forest reduction, the isotopy type is determined by the endpoint pairing/crossing pattern. A reviewer requested that this be justified explicitly.
In excluding cells of dimension at least $3$, the proof should more explicitly note that multiple intersections between the same two intervals are already ruled out by the forest/no-cycle argument.

Several reviewer comments concern style and presentation: unusual section headings inside a proof, superfluous adverbs, the absence of pictures, and optional simplifications of the enumeration or the final observation that the complex is homeomorphic to $S^2$.

verdict_rationale: The proof has a load-bearing unproved assertion: the formula (1) is asserted to produce a complete flag of valuated matroids with adjacent quotient relations, but the referees agree that the cited literature does not supply this relative valuated Higgs lift and the submission gives no proof. This gap is needed to prove that the polar transform even maps the relative Dressian to itself, so the main theorem is not established.

errors.title: Unproved relative valuated Higgs completion
errors.errored_block:
Finally, if $\nu\preceq\mu_M$ has rank $k$, we use its valuated Higgs
completion
\[
 h_j(B)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min\{\nu(C): B\subseteq C,\ |C|=k\}, & j\le k,\ |B|=j,\\
 \min\{\nu(C): C\subseteq B,\ |C|=k\}, & j\ge k,\ B\in\mathcal I_j(M),\\
 \infty, & j\ge k,\ B\notin\mathcal I_j(M).
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{1}
\]
Murota's truncation and relative elongation theorems \cite[Theorems 2.1 and 4.1]{Murota}, equivalently the
Dress--Terhalle well-layering construction \cite{DT}, give valuated matroids
$h_j$ and adjacent quotients $h_j\preceq h_{j+1}$.
errors.block_location: Section 0, paragraph defining the valuated Higgs completion (equation (1))
errors.error_description: The proof defines functions $h_j$ by the displayed minimization formula and then asserts, by citation, that these are valuated matroids satisfying adjacent quotient relations $h_j\preceq h_{j+1}$. The referees state that the cited results do not prove this relative valuated Higgs lift for a general matroid $M$, and the submission itself gives no proof of the valuated Plücker relations for the $h_j$ or of the incidence/quotient relations between adjacent layers. This is not merely a citation problem: Proposition \ref{prop:set} begins by inserting an arbitrary $\nu$ into this alleged complete flag and its induction uses $h_j\preceq h_{j+1}$, so without this construction the proof does not establish that $\nu^{\perp_M}$ lies in $\Dr(M)$ or that the final order-reversing involution is defined on the relative Dressian.

secondary_issues.description: Several referees note that the citations to Murota and Dress--Terhalle for the Higgs completion are bogus or misleading; this citation failure accompanies the mathematical gap above rather than resolving it.
Reviewer 1 says the citation for the cocircuit-generation theorem of tropical linear spaces as the closed tropical convex hull of valuated cocircuits is wrong.

The proof of the nested-incidence criterion is considered confusing: one reviewer objected to the final inference to orthogonality with $c$, while another said the statement is known and the proof is essentially correct but poorly organized and should explicitly frame the argument in terms of covectors and circuits.

Reviewer comments also flag terminology and presentation issues, such as the undefined phrase “projective valuated matroid,” the use of “vector” where “covector” may be intended, missing displayed equations in the elementary opposition lemma, and the need to specify that closures in the polar definition are closures in $M$.

verdict_rationale: The proof contains essential unjustified gaps in the proof of the local rank-three Pluecker reduction and, more seriously, in the annihilator lemma where a basis/apartment restriction principle is used without being stated or proved. There is also a minor projective-cone convention error involving the all-infinity vector. Many other referee remarks are matters of exposition or organization rather than mathematical defects.

errors.title: All-infinity vector incorrectly treated as a projective tropical point
errors.errored_block: We first show \(w\in\Trop([Z,Y])\).  Let \(D\) be a circuit of this geometry, choose a basis \(A\) of \(Z\), and choose \(e_P\in P\setminus Z\) for \(P\in D\).  A circuit of the contraction by \(Z\) lifts to an \(M\)-circuit \(C\subseteq Z\cup\{e_P:P\in D\}\) whose image is \(D\).  Applying Lemma \ref{lem:quotient} to \(C\) and \(A\), the elements in \(Z\) contribute \(\infty\), and the remaining values are \(w(P)\).  Thus \(w\in\Trop([Z,Y])\).
errors.error_description: The proof concludes that the vector \(w\) lies in the projective tropical linear space \(\Trop([Z,Y])\). However, it is possible that all values \(w(P)=\bar p(P)\) are \(\infty\); then \(w\) is the all-\(\infty\) vector, which is excluded from projective tropical space under the conventions stated at the beginning of the proof. The intended argument can likely be repaired by treating this case separately, where the desired minimum is trivially all \(\infty\), or by explicitly working in the affine cone, but as written the membership assertion is not strictly correct.

errors.title: Rank-three matching case check is asserted rather than proved
errors.errored_block:
If none of the \(L_i\) equals \(B\), color \(L_i\) by \(y_i=L_i\wedge B\).  A pair \(L_i,L_j\) meets on \(B\) exactly when \(y_i=y_j\); otherwise its contribution is \(0\).  For four colored objects, by the multiplicities \(1+1+1+1,2+1+1,2+2,3+1,4\), the minimum over the three perfect matchings is never unique.  If, say, \(L_1=B\), put \(y_i=L_i\wedge B\) for \(i=2,3,4\) and \(c(y)=\lambda+\mu\) for \(y=a\), \(c(y)=\mu\) otherwise.  The three costs are
\[
c(y_2)+{\bf 1}_{y_3=y_4}c(y_3),\quad
c(y_3)+{\bf 1}_{y_2=y_4}c(y_2),\quad
c(y_4)+{\bf 1}_{y_2=y_3}c(y_2),
\]
and the cases ``all distinct'', ``exactly two equal'', and ``all equal'' give, respectively, at least two minimal costs, the two costs pairing \(B\) with one of the equal colors, or three equal costs.
errors.block_location: Lemma \ref{lem:local}, proof of the elementary rank-three fact
errors.error_description: This passage is the only proof of the key rank-three fact used to establish the local dual Pluecker relation in the case \(\rk(Z)=k-1\). It replaces the needed verification with a compressed coloring argument and an undeveloped list of multiplicity cases. As the referees note, the finite case check may be fillable, but the proof as written does not actually justify that the three matching costs can never have a unique finite minimum in all configurations of the lines and all possible weights \(\lambda,\mu\), including infinite values. Since Lemma \ref{lem:local} is then invoked to prove that \(p^\dagger\) satisfies the tropical Pluecker relations, this leaves a substantive gap in the construction.

errors.title: Unproved basis/apartment restriction principle in the annihilator lemma
errors.errored_block: Since \(B\mapsto B^*\) is a bijection on \(M\)-bases, the previous paragraph says that \(x\) satisfies the defining equations of \(p^\dagger\) on every Boolean apartment coming from an \(M\)-basis.  Let \(J\in\binomE{n+1}\), where \(n=\rk(p^\dagger)\).  If \(J\) is independent, extend it to an \(M\)-basis and use the apartment calculation.  If \(\rk_M(J)\le n-1\), all \(n\)-subsets \(J-j\) are dependent.  If \(\rk_M(J)=n\), then \(J\) has a unique circuit \(D\); the finite coefficients \(p^\dagger_{J-j}\) occur exactly for \(j\in D\), and for those \(j\) the flats \(\cl_M(J-j)\) are equal.  The equation is therefore the circuit equation for \(D\), satisfied by \(x\in\Trop(M)\).  Hence \(x\in\Trop(p^\dagger)\).
errors.block_location: Lemma \ref{lem:annihilator}, converse direction of the annihilator formula
errors.error_description: The proof uses an unstated principle that satisfying the relevant equations after restriction to every basis, or “Boolean apartment,” suffices to satisfy the defining equations of the global tropical linear space. The same kind of reduction is also used in the forward direction to pass from equations on each \(M\)-basis to the inclusion \(\Trop(p)\subseteq\Trop(x^\dagger)\). As the referees explain, such a step requires a separate justification in terms of valuated circuit/orthogonality or incidence relations for valuated matroid quotients; it is not enough merely to say that an independent set can be extended to a basis and to invoke an undefined apartment calculation. Without this missing lemma, the equivalence in Lemma \ref{lem:annihilator} is not proved, and the later definition of the involution on tropical linear spaces is not fully justified.

secondary_issues.description: The overview says that modularity implies flat constancy of valuated quotients, but the referees point out that this constancy does not depend on modularity; the statement is misleading as an explanation of the proof structure rather than a mathematical obstruction.
Several comments concern presentation only: the theorem name “Established finite-ground-set theorem,” the notation \(\TP^{E-1}\), and the terminology “Boolean apartment” are unclear or nonstandard.

The referees note that several routine arguments, such as the quotient criterion, reduction to simplification, and ordinary support construction inside Lemma \ref{lem:daggerquotient}, could be shortened or isolated as separate lemmas; these are organizational issues rather than mathematical errors.

verdict_rationale: The submission proves some preliminary lattice and flat-invariance facts, but the central “modular-lattice valuated duality” theorem is not actually proved. The proof relies on nonstandard/undefined equivalences and merely asserts the two hard parts: that the pulled-back flat-valued function is a valuated quotient, and that the construction reverses quotient/flag incidence. Since the main theorem depends on these assertions, the proof of the desired involution is incomplete.

errors.title: Unproved construction of the dual valuated quotient
errors.errored_block: By Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-invariance}, every valuated quotient \(p\) of a modular matroid \(M\) is equivalently a valuated matroid on the modular lattice \(\cL(M)\), with coordinates indexed by rank-\(s\) flats.  The tropical Plucker relations are local relations in length-four intervals of \(\cL(M)\), and the tropical incidence relations for a pair of quotients are the corresponding local flag-Plucker relations.  An order-reversing lattice isomorphism sends length-four intervals to length-four intervals and interchanges rank \(s\) with rank \(d-s\).  Therefore pulling the flat-valued Plucker coordinates back along \(F\mapsto F^\perp\) preserves the tropical Plucker relations and reverses the flag incidence relations.
errors.error_description: This passage is supposed to prove that \(\bar p^{\perp}\) is the flat-valued form of a rank-\((d-s)\) valuated quotient of \(M\), but it only gives a vague assertion. Lemma \ref{lem:flat-invariance} shows constancy of \(p\) on bases of the same flat; it does not establish an equivalence with a well-defined theory of “valuated matroids on the modular lattice,” nor does it prove that pulling back along the lattice anti-isomorphism satisfies the valuated matroid axioms. In particular, the proof omits the necessary verification that the finite-support sets of \(p^\perp\) form a matroid and that all relevant tropical exchange relations, including degenerate cases beyond length-four intervals, hold. This leaves the existence of \(p^\perp\) as a valuated quotient unproved, which is a central step of the argument.

errors.title: Unjustified reversal of quotient/flag incidence
errors.errored_block: Finally, the valuated flag relation \(q\twoheadrightarrow p\) is carried to \(p^\perp\twoheadrightarrow q^\perp\), which is precisely the asserted reversal of containment of tropical linear spaces.
errors.error_description: The theorem needs compatibility with quotients: from a valuated quotient relation \(q\twoheadrightarrow p\), one must prove that the constructed duals satisfy \(p^\perp\twoheadrightarrow q^\perp\). This sentence simply asserts that the valuated flag relation is carried to the reversed one, without checking the tropical incidence/flag-Plucker relations for the dual pair. The later proof that \(\Phi\) is order-reversing depends exactly on this unproved compatibility, so the main order-reversal claim is not established.

secondary_issues.description: Several references are presented as supporting statements they apparently do not contain, including the citations for the valuated flag matroid correspondence and especially the cited literature for the purported modular-lattice valuated duality theorem.

The proof misleadingly describes the modular-lattice duality formalism as “standard” and says “We recall the argument,” although the reviewers indicate that this is not a standard result and requires a substantive proof.

Some parts are unnecessarily verbose or redundant, such as the proof of the lattice modularity lemma and the inclusion of point (iii) in Theorem \ref{thm:modular-duality}, which reviewers note follows from other assertions and standard quotient facts if those assertions were proved.

verdict_rationale: The proof attempts to disprove a statement that the referees identify as true. Its central cardinality argument fails because it counts only ordinary/unvaluated matroid quotients and falsely excludes infinitely many valuated quotients or elementary lifts containing the specified boundary point.

errors.title: False exhaustion of valuated rank-2 quotients by four rigid ordinary topologies
errors.errored_block: This explicitly exhausts the unvaluated topologies. None of these four topologies ($S_{L_1}, V_{\{1\}}, V_{\{2\}}, V_{\{3\}}$) admit internal valuated edges that maintain the $e_{123}$ ray, because any internal split would necessitate intermediate parallel groupings (e.g., size $2$ subsets of $\{4,5,6,7\}$) which do not correspond to valid flats of $F_7$. Consequently, they exist precisely as four isolated, rigid trees.
errors.block_location: Step 3, final paragraph after the enumeration
errors.error_description: This paragraph moves from an enumeration of four ordinary, unvaluated quotient types to the much stronger claim that there are no nontrivial valuated deformations and hence only four rigid tropical lines in the relevant filter. The referees point out that this confuses ordinary matroid quotients with valuated matroid quotients: even if the ordinary quotients are four, there are infinitely many valuated quotients of the Fano matroid. Thus the asserted exhaustion of the relevant tropical lines is false, and the later finite cardinality count is unsupported.

errors.title: False dismissal of elementary or continuous lifts containing the boundary point
errors.errored_block: A known theoretical failure mode involves assuming that continuous $1$-parameter families of trees (such as $T_{L_1, l}$, which locally splits $\{1,2,3\}$ from $\{4,5,6,7\}$ along an internal edge) contain $V_{L_1}$, thereby generating $\mathfrak{c}$ elements and dissolving the contradiction. This is geometrically false. To physically encompass $V_{L_1}$, a tree must achieve coordinates where $x_1=x_2=x_3=\infty$ \emph{simultaneously}. In the split family $T_{L_1, l}$, the leaves $1$, $2$, and $3$ are separated by the internal vertex and diverge along independent infinite rays $e_1, e_2, e_3$. Consequently, their geometric limits trace to the three distinct boundary points where exactly \emph{one} coordinate is infinite (i.e., $V_{\{1\}}, V_{\{2\}}, V_{\{3\}}$). The strict boundary point $V_{L_1}$ is never reached by this family.
errors.error_description: The proof asserts that the relevant one-parameter split families do not contain $V_{L_1}$ and, in effect, that $V_{L_1}$ has no elementary lifts of the needed sort. Reviewer 2 identifies this as absurd: such elementary lifts or valuated deformations do exist. The coordinate-limit discussion does not justify excluding these tropical lines from the filter, so this step incorrectly removes the very continuous families that would invalidate the proposed cardinality contradiction.

errors.title: Invalid cardinality contradiction and wrong final conclusion
errors.errored_block:
Because all continuous families structurally miss $V_{L_1}$, the count is strictly locked at $|F(V_{L_1})| = 4$. The assumed involution $\Phi$ demands a bijection between the point ideal $I(V_{\{1\}})$ (cardinality $\mathfrak{c}$) and the filter of containing lines $F(V_{L_1})$ (cardinality $4$). Since $4 \neq \mathfrak{c}$, no such order-reversing bijection can exist on the relative Dressian. 
Therefore, there is no order-reversing involution $\Phi$ extending $F \mapsto F^\perp$.
errors.error_description: The final contradiction depends on the asserted equality $|F(V_{L_1})|=4$, but the referees explain that the relevant filter is not limited to four elements: there are infinitely many valuated quotients, despite there being only four ordinary matroid quotients in the calculation. Consequently the claimed cardinality mismatch is false. Moreover, the referees state that the desired order-reversing duality statement is true, so the proof reaches the wrong conclusion rather than producing a valid counterexample.

secondary_issues.description: The proof relies on a specific labeling of the Fano matroid but does not give a diagram or list of lines/circuits, making the later flat calculations hard to verify.

Several pieces of terminology are unclear or nonstandard in the submission, including “principal ideal of points,” “infinite point,” “initial matroid at infinity,” “unvaluated topologies,” and the discussion of “prior misconceptions regarding deformations.”

Reviewer 2 notes that the ordinary quotient classification is presented in an unnecessarily obscure way; for the Fano matroid it could be derived more simply using modular cuts and principal truncations.

verdict_rationale: The referees agree that the mathematical argument and the stated combinatorial formula are correct. The comments raise citation, organization, wording, and at most a trivial edge-case clarification, but no substantive mathematical defect in the proof for the intended positive values of n.

secondary_issues.description: The proof uses diagonal supersymmetry and the Rhoades--Wilson Hilbert series formula but does not give sufficiently explicit in-text citations or theorem references; reviewers note that these are recent results rather than merely “standard inputs.”
The formula for the super Schur polynomial in one even and one odd variable is stated without a reference.

Several explanatory phrases are confusing or under-defined, including the statement that the coefficients are stable multiplicities of GL_m-irreducibles, the phrase “purely bosonic expansion,” and the assertion that a partition lies in the “(1,1)-hook.”

Reviewers recommend breaking the dense single proof into separate lemmas or theorem statements for the diagonal supersymmetry input, the Rhoades--Wilson formula, and the combinatorial interpretation of the q-Stirling recurrence.

Reviewer 2 notes that the k=0 term in the Rhoades--Wilson formula would matter only for the trivial edge case n=0 and suggests addressing this explicitly; this does not affect the proof for the intended n≥1 range.

verdict_rationale: The referees uniformly judge the mathematical content and final formula to be correct. The substantive comments concern citation precision, explaining equivalence to a differently stated known formula, and exposition/streamlining rather than false mathematical steps or an incomplete proof.

secondary_issues.description: The displayed Fields Frobenius formula is attributed to Murai--Rhoades--Wilson, but the referees note that it does not appear in that paper in exactly this form. They regard it as equivalent by a routine calculation, so this is not a mathematical error, but the paper should either prove the equivalence or cite a source/formulation more precisely.

Several standard facts are reproved without acknowledging their classical status, notably the one-variable super Schur specialization and the Gaussian/binomial identities including the q-Pascal identity. Referees suggest citing standard references or stating that these are classical.

The derivation of the Hilbert series by first passing through the Frobenius characteristic is longer than necessary; referees point out that an existing Rhoades--Wilson Hilbert series formula could simplify the argument. This is a matter of presentation, not correctness.

Some wording and notation choices were criticized as distracting or unnecessary, including the term “headline theorem,” switching between d/M and des/maj notation, the undefined reference to a “Delta expression,” and explaining trivial algebra such as (d-1)-b=d-b-1.

verdict_rationale: The stated formula and the ordered-set-partition/q-series manipulations are accepted by the referees as mathematically correct. The only genuine mathematical defect is that the hook-specialization lemma relies on an asserted identification between ordinary diagonal coinvariants and the superspace coinvariant ring without proving or properly citing the required functorial/universality result. The remaining referee comments are citation, notation, or exposition issues.

errors.title: Unjustified passage from diagonal coinvariants to the superspace coinvariant ring
errors.errored_block:
The construction of diagonal coinvariants is functorial in the row-space. For a
purely even row-space of dimension \(m\), its character is
\[
\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n)s_\lambda(q_1,\dots,q_m).
\]
Evaluating the same polynomial functor on a \(1|1\)-dimensional superspace gives
the superspace coinvariant ring \(SR_n\).
errors.block_location: Section “Superspace and hook extraction”, proof of Lemma “Hook specialization”
errors.error_description: The proof asserts that the same polynomial functor whose purely even evaluations give the multivariate diagonal coinvariant Hilbert series also evaluates on a \(1|1\)-dimensional superspace to the superspace coinvariant ring \(SR_n\). This is the key universality/diagonal-supersymmetry step needed to transfer the coefficients \(c_\lambda(n)\) from \(R_n^{(m)}\) to \(SR_n\), but it is only stated informally and not proved or supported by the appropriate reference. Without this identification, the later equality \(\Hilb(SR_n;q,z)=1+(q+z)C_n(q,z)\) is not established, so the extraction of the hook coefficients from the Rhoades--Wilson Hilbert series has a gap.

secondary_issues.description: Several references are inaccurate or missing: the Rhoades--Wilson formula is cited to a nonexistent Theorem 1.1 and to an equation that is a conjecture in the introduction rather than to the later theorem proving it; the ordered-set-partition/q-Stirling result should acknowledge known work such as Steingrímsson and Remmel--Wilson; and the superspace identification should cite the appropriate diagonal supersymmetry source.

Some notation and terminology should be clarified, including the meaning of \((\Omega_n)^{\mathfrak S_n}_+\), the symbol \(hs_{(a\mid b)}\), which character and diagonal coinvariant construction are being invoked, and the initial condition for the Carlitz \(q\)-Stirling numbers.

The reviewers also noted stylistic issues: “hook formula” is a potentially misleading title because of the classical hook formula, and the inversion statistic is technically correct but presented in an unusual way.

verdict_rationale: The proof has substantial mathematical defects: it sets up the polynomial ring with the wrong representation dimension, uses undefined and unproved “evaluation at a superspace” operations to pass to hooks and to a super-coinvariant algebra, and the final claimed combinatorial interpretation depends on an undefined basis and an unproved multiplicity count. These are not merely citation or wording issues; they prevent the argument from proving the requested combinatorial interpretation.

errors.title: Wrong representation dimension for the variables
errors.errored_block: Let $\mathbb{C}[X] = \operatorname{Sym}(V \otimes E)$ be the polynomial ring representing $m$ sets of $n$ variables, where $V$ is the $(n-1)$-dimensional standard representation of $S_n$ and $E = \mathbb{C}^m$.
errors.error_description: The proof identifies the polynomial ring for $m$ sets of $n$ variables with $\operatorname{Sym}(V\otimes E)$ while taking $V$ to be $(n-1)$-dimensional. As the reviewers point out, this would represent $m$ sets of only $n-1$ variables, not the coinvariant algebra with $m$ sets of $n$ variables appearing in the problem. This incorrect initial model means the subsequent quotient is not the stated algebra $R_n^{(m)}$ as written.

errors.title: Undefined superspace evaluation does not justify isolating hook coefficients
errors.errored_block: To strictly isolate the hook shape partitions $\lambda = (k, 1^d)$, we evaluate the $GL_m$ character at the superspace $E = \mathbb{C}^{1|1}$ (one commuting variable $q$, one anti-commuting variable $z$). In this space, the Schur functor $S^\lambda(\mathbb{C}^{1|1})$ evaluates to zero for all non-hook shapes.
errors.error_description: The argument claims that one can evaluate a $GL_m$ character at the superspace $\mathbb{C}^{1|1}$ and thereby isolate precisely the hook terms. No mathematical definition of this evaluation is given; if the intended operation is passage to super Schur functions or Schur functors on a super vector space, the needed vanishing criterion for non-hooks and the recovery of the individual coefficients $c_{(k,1^d)}(n)$ are not proved. Thus the central reduction from the ordinary Schur expansion to hook coefficients is left unjustified.

errors.title: Unjustified identification of an evaluated coinvariant algebra with the super-coinvariant algebra
errors.errored_block:
Evaluating $R_n^{(m)}$ at $E = \mathbb{C}^{1|1}$ maps the generators of the multi-symmetric invariant ideal $I$ (the polarizations of the power sums $p_r$) directly to $p_r(x)$ and their fermionic derivations $\sum x_i^{r-1} \theta_i$. This quotient is mathematically identical to the super-coinvariant algebra 
    \[
    SR_n = \mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n] \otimes \Lambda(\theta_1, \dots, \theta_n) / \left\langle p_r(x), \sum x_i^{r-1} \theta_i \right\rangle.
    \]
errors.error_description: The proof treats $R_n^{(m)}$ as something that can be “evaluated” at a super vector space $E=\mathbb{C}^{1|1}$, but no such functorial construction or substitution is defined. It also does not prove that the multisymmetric invariant ideal maps exactly to the ideal generated by the stated power sums and fermionic derivations. Consequently, the claimed identification with the super-coinvariant algebra $SR_n$ is an unsupported step, so later conclusions about hook coefficients via $SR_n$ do not follow.

errors.title: Final count is not a well-defined combinatorial interpretation
errors.errored_block: \textbf{Combinatorial Interpretation:} The universal coefficient $c_{(k, 1^d)}(n)$ exactly enumerates the number of Ordered Set Partitions of $[n]$ that act as highest-weight ``sources'' (elements annihilated by the fermionic derivation operator in the OSP combinatorial basis of $SR_n$) possessing exactly a polynomial degree of $k$ and an exterior degree of $d$.
errors.error_description: The announced interpretation relies on an “OSP combinatorial basis of $SR_n$,” a fermionic derivation operator on that basis, and a class of highest-weight “sources,” but these objects are not defined or established. The proof also gives no argument that the number of such annihilated basis elements equals the relevant Schur coefficient. Therefore the final sentence does not provide a genuine combinatorial formula for $c_{(k,1^d)}(n)$; it is an unproved and vague algebraic restatement.

secondary_issues.description: The notation $s_\lambda(E)$ and the phrase “super-Schur module” are not explained clearly enough for the representation-theoretic claims to be checked.

The cited attribution to Haglund--Rhoades--Shimozono for the total dimension of $SR_n$ is wrong or at least misleading; one reviewer notes that the relevant dimension result is proved in work of Rhoades--Wilson instead.
The submission is explicitly presented as a partial proof and is written as a list of ideas, with several key constructions and operators left undefined.

verdict_rationale: The overall strategy is regarded by the referees as plausible and possibly correct after substantial rewriting, but the proof as written has genuine mathematical gaps. In particular, a key support-bookkeeping lemma uses an asserted commutation of support projections whose proof is wrong, and later applications of DKEP results conflate Hilbert-space correspondences with the operator-bimodule framework required by those results. These gaps support later claims about boundary supports and coefficient compactness, so the submitted proof is not complete as written.

errors.title: Unsupported commutation of hereditary support with one-normal supports
errors.errored_block:
Apply the same one-normal support statement to \(Y\) for each of the two
normal structures.  The faithfulness hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis
needed there for the multiplier actions on \(Y\).  Thus \(r_Y\) commutes with
both \(p_\ell\) and \(p_r\), and the two one-normal biduals of \(Y\) are
\(r_Yp_\ell A_N^{**}p_\ell r_Y\) and \(r_Yp_rA_N^{**}p_rr_Y\).  Applying
Proposition 2.10 to the inclusion \(Y\subset A_N\) and using the elementary
intersection formula once more gives
\[
        (Y^{\sharp_J})^*
        = r_Yp_NA_N^{**}p_Nr_Y
        = (p_Nr_Y)\,\cA_N\,(p_Nr_Y).
\]
errors.error_description: The proof asserts that applying the one-normal support statement to the hereditary subalgebra \(Y\) implies that its ordinary open support \(r_Y\) commutes with the one-normal support projections \(p_\ell\) and \(p_r\). Reviewer 3 explicitly says this proof is wrong, and Reviewer 2 identifies a gap in this lemma. Faithfulness of the multiplier actions does not by itself justify this commutation in the ordinary bidual. Without the commutation, the displayed corner formula \((Y^{\sharp_J})^*=(p_Nr_Y)\cA_N(p_Nr_Y)\) and the support identity \(q_X=p_Nr_X=p_N\rho_X\) are not established, and those identities are later used in the intersection-of-supports argument.

errors.title: Misapplication of DKEP Theorem 5.10 to a Hilbert correspondence instead of the required operator-bimodule framework
errors.errored_block:
The conjugation \(\overline{\xi\otimes_B\bar\eta}\mapsto
\eta\otimes_B\bar\xi\) gives \(\overline{\cH_B}\cong\cH_B\).  Let
\(\mathcal C\) be the elementary bounded tensors in \(\cH_B\).  They are
\(N\)-\(N\) cyclic, and \(T_\alpha\in X_B\subset X_BA_NX_B\) for
\(\alpha\in\mathcal C\).  Hence DKEP Theorem 5.10(1) applies, so \(\cH_B\) is
mixing relative to \(X_B\times X_B\).
errors.error_description: The proof invokes DKEP Theorem 5.10(1) directly for the Hilbert-space correspondence \(\cH_B\). Reviewer 3 points out that Theorem 5.10 is formulated for operator bimodules, not for Hilbert space bimodules in this unqualified form. The proof never constructs or identifies the relevant operator bimodule associated with \(\cH_B\), nor checks that the coefficient-operator condition is the one required by DKEP. Therefore the conclusion that \(\cH_B\) is mixing relative to \(X_B\times X_B\), and hence the later coefficient-compactness conclusion for direct sums of \(\cH_B\), is not justified as written.

errors.title: Finite-fusion calculus relies on the same unestablished correspondence/operator-bimodule identification
errors.errored_block:
For a mixing correspondence \(H\), Theorem 5.10 says that
\[
  \mathcal C_H=\{\xi\in H_{\rm b}: T_\xi\in X A_N X\}
\]
is \(N\)-\(N\) cyclic.  Direct sums are handled by placing the cyclic vectors
in one summand; their span contains the finite-support algebraic sum and is
dense, while the coefficient condition is unchanged.  If \(H\) and \(K\) are
mixing and \(\xi\in\mathcal C_H,\eta\in\mathcal C_K\), then \(\xi\otimes_N\eta\)
is bounded, such elementary tensors are cyclic for \(H\otimes_NK\), and
\[
        T_{\xi\otimes\eta}=T_\eta T_\xi\in (X A_N X)(X A_N X)\subset X A_N X,
\]
because \(X\) is hereditary.  Thus the cyclic-vector criterion proves mixing
for fusions.
errors.error_description: This argument again states DKEP Theorem 5.10 as a criterion for Hilbert correspondences and then uses it to prove stability of mixing under Connes fusion. The referees note that the relevant DKEP result concerns operator bimodules and that the proof is missing the operator-bimodule input needed to translate between that setting and the Hilbert correspondences being fused. Consequently, the cyclic-vector criterion and the asserted preservation of mixing under fusion are not justified in the framework actually cited, which affects the subsequent claim that all bounded-vector coefficients in such finite fusions lie in \(K_X(N)\).

secondary_issues.description: Several terms such as “ordinary support,” “one-normal support,” and “compact hereditary algebra” are unclear or not standard as written. Reviewer 2 notes that “compact hereditary algebra” is not DKEP terminology, and Reviewers 1 and 3 found the terminology hard to parse. These are primarily presentation/definition issues unless tied to the specific mathematical gaps listed above.
Reviewer 2 says the sentence about ruling out central states with normal restriction contains unnecessary wording (“normal” and “after normalization”); this does not affect the mathematics.

Reviewer 3 says the phrase “elementary intersection formula” is unclear and that the symbols \(A\) and \(B\) in the fusion-rule display are not clearly introduced. These are clarity issues in otherwise plausible parts of the argument.

Reviewer 3 notes that one citation to Theorem 5.10 does not name the paper, and Reviewer 2 notes some DKEP terminology is inaccurately named. These are attribution/citation defects rather than independent mathematical errors.

Reviewers 1 and 2 repeatedly state that Lemmas \ref{lem:subalg}, \ref{lem:fusion}, and \ref{lem:intersection} need substantial rewriting and clarification, although Reviewer 2 regards the essential ideas of Lemmas \ref{lem:subalg}, \ref{lem:fusion}, and \ref{lem:intersection} as correct and Reviewer 3 says the intersection lemma is generally correct but misses a simplifying consequence.

verdict_rationale: The submission does not prove the graph-product theorem in the problem. It explicitly replaces the target statement by an abstract conditional upgrade lemma, and even that lemma is formulated using nonstandard or incorrect DKEP terminology and definitions. The actual graph-product boundary construction, support relations, and relative proper proximality hypotheses are assumed rather than proved.

errors.title: The proof explicitly proves a different, conditional statement rather than the requested graph-product theorem
errors.errored_block: This write-up proves the following \textbf{abstract DKEP finite-cover upgrade lemma}, not the full graph-product theorem stated above. Thus it is a relaxation/different result: it assumes the relevant DKEP boundary pieces, support projections, support sandwich inequality, and relative proper proximality as hypotheses, and proves only the final upgrade from relative proper proximality for finitely many pieces to absolute proper proximality.
errors.error_description: The original problem asks for a proof that an irreducible graph product von Neumann algebra with trace-zero unitaries at the vertices is properly proximal. This block explicitly states that the submission does not prove that theorem, but instead proves an abstract finite-cover upgrade lemma under additional hypotheses. The subsequent proof never derives the required DKEP boundary pieces, support projections, support sandwich inequality, relative proper proximality, or absence of amenable direct summand from the graph-product assumptions. Consequently the proof establishes, at most, a different conditional statement and leaves the requested theorem unproved.

errors.title: The ambient DKEP compactification is not mathematically specified
errors.errored_block: Assume \(M\) is placed in the DKEP properly proximal framework: there is a unital von Neumann algebra \(\mathcal N\), called the normal-bidual compactification, containing the left copy of \(M\) and containing support projections for DKEP boundary pieces.
errors.block_location: Problem Solved, setup of the abstract lemma
errors.error_description: The proof invokes a von Neumann algebra \(\mathcal N\) called the “normal-bidual compactification,” but this is not standard terminology and the object is not explicitly defined. Since the obstruction state, weak-* support projections, and order inequalities are all supposed to live in this algebra, the proof needs a precise identification of \(\mathcal N\) and of how the relevant boundary pieces and supports sit inside it. Without that, the stated black-box obstruction theorem and the later inequalities are not well-defined in the claimed DKEP framework.

errors.title: The definition of a DKEP boundary piece is misstated
errors.errored_block: A DKEP boundary piece \(X\subset B(H)\) means a hereditary \(C^*\)-subalgebra, invariant under the left and right \(M\)-actions, whose elements are treated as \(X\)-compact operators.
errors.block_location: Problem Solved, setup of the abstract lemma
errors.error_description: The proof identifies DKEP boundary pieces with hereditary \(C^*\)-subalgebras invariant under the full left and right actions of \(M\). According to the referee, in the DKEP framework such boundary pieces are not necessarily invariant under the full von Neumann algebra \(M\), but only under the left and right action of a specified ultraweakly dense \(C^*\)-subalgebra. Thus the proof uses an incorrect version of a basic object, so the later notions of relative proper proximality and the obstruction theorem are not being applied to the standard DKEP boundary pieces.

errors.title: The boundary pieces indexed by the abstract sets are simply assumed, not constructed from the graph product
errors.errored_block: For every \(U\in\mathcal F\), suppose there is a DKEP boundary piece \(X_U\) with support projection \(q_U\in\mathcal N\). Assume \(q_{\varnothing}=q_K\).
errors.error_description: The sets \(U\) are introduced abstractly, but the proof gives no construction associating them to boundary pieces for the graph product von Neumann algebra in the original theorem. The existence of \(X_U\), the support projections \(q_U\), and especially the identification \(q_{\varnothing}=q_K\) are imposed as hypotheses rather than derived from the irreducible graph-product assumptions. This is precisely one of the substantive parts needed for the original theorem, so the argument is incomplete as a proof of that theorem.

errors.title: The key support-intersection inequality is assumed rather than proved
errors.errored_block:
Assume also the support sandwich inequality
\[
q_Uq_Wq_U\le q_{U\cap W}
\]
in the positive order of \(\mathcal N\), for all \(U,W\in\mathcal F\).
errors.error_description: The proof relies on this support sandwich inequality to pass from support one on \(q_U\) and \(q_W\) to support one on \(q_{U\cap W}\). But for the graph-product theorem, establishing such support-intersection relations is part of the main technical difficulty; the referee notes that in the relevant setting this condition even forces the commutation relation \([q_U,q_W]=0\). Since the original graph-product hypotheses do not include this inequality and the proof never proves it, the central step of the proposed argument is assumed rather than established.

errors.title: The small-at-infinity algebra defining relative proper proximality is incorrect
errors.errored_block:
For a boundary piece \(X\), define
\[
S_X(M)=\{T\in B(H):[T,\rho(x)]\in X\text{ for every }x\in M\}.
\]
A state \(\psi\) on \(S_X(M)\) is \(M\)-central if \(\psi(xT)=\psi(Tx)\) for all \(x\in M\), \(T\in S_X(M)\). The algebra \(M\) is properly proximal relative to \(X\) if there is no \(M\)-central state on \(S_X(M)\) whose restriction to the left copy of \(M\) is normal.
errors.block_location: Problem Solved, definition of relative proper proximality
errors.error_description: The proof defines \(S_X(M)\) by requiring \([T,\rho(x)]\in X\) for every \(x\in M\). In the DKEP framework, as the referee explains, the condition should be membership in the \(L^\infty\)-\(L^1\) closure \(\overline{X}^{\infty,1}\), not necessarily in \(X\) itself. This changes the algebra on which central states are tested and therefore changes the meaning of relative proper proximality. Consequently the black-box obstruction theorem quoted later cannot be applied to the object defined here.

secondary_issues.description: The proof repeatedly invokes DKEP and a DKEP obstruction theorem without precise citations, theorem numbers, or standard notation, making it difficult to verify the claimed black-box inputs.

Reviewers noted that Sections 1 and 2 prove only elementary state-support facts and do not address the substantive graph-product difficulties; this is primarily a matter of mathematical weight and presentation rather than an independent error in those elementary arguments.

verdict_rationale: The proof’s overall strategy is plausible, but the main theorem is not proved. The upgrading lemma contains an invalid projection argument and is false as stated without additional commutation hypotheses, and the boundary-cover lemma is essentially asserted rather than proved. These are central steps used in the final argument.

errors.title: Invalid upgrade from individual support projections to their meet
errors.errored_block:
For each $i$, if $\varphi(q_i^\perp)>0$, then the normalized compression of $\varphi$ by $q_i^\perp$ gives an $M$-central state on the small-at-infinity system relative to $X_i$, still normal on $M$, contradicting relative proper proximality.  Hence $\varphi(q_i)=1$ for all $i$.  Since the $q_i$ are central projections and the family is finite,
\[
\varphi\Big(\bigwedge_i q_i\Big)=1.
\]
errors.error_description: The proof asserts that the support projections $q_i$ are central projections and uses this to conclude that a state satisfying $\varphi(q_i)=1$ for each $i$ must satisfy $\varphi(\bigwedge_i q_i)=1$. The reviewers point out that these support projections are not central in general, and Lemma \ref{lem:upgrade} is wrong as stated without at least an additional commutation hypothesis. Moreover, the proof does not justify that $\varphi(q_i^\perp)$ is even defined in the relevant compact-boundary bidual system, nor that $\varphi$ has the normality properties needed to pass to a meet of noncommuting projections. Thus the contradiction with $\varphi(q_{\K})=0$ is not established, so the upgrading lemma does not prove proper proximality.

errors.title: Boundary-cover meet formula for graph-product support projections is not proved
errors.errored_block:
The first assertion is the support-projection form of the graph-product bimodule calculation for subgraph algebras; see Charlesworth--de Santiago--Hayes--Jekel--Kunnawalkam Elayavalli--Nelson \cite[Theorem 0.4, Theorem 5.4, and Proposition 5.5]{CDHJKEN}.  Equivalently, the $M$-$M$ boundary piece generated by $e_{M_U}$ intersects/fuses with the one generated by $e_{M_W}$ exactly as the subgraph algebras intersect:
\[
M_U\cap M_W=M_{U\cap W},
\qquad
E_U E_W=E_{U\cap W}.
\]
Iterating gives the formula for finitely many $U_i$.
errors.error_description: The proof claims that the meet formula $q_{U_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge q_{U_n}=q_{U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_n}$ follows from a “graph-product bimodule calculation” and from the identities $M_U\cap M_W=M_{U\cap W}$ and $E_UE_W=E_{U\cap W}$. The reviewers state that the cited results do not directly compute these $M$-$M$ boundary pieces or their support projections, and that the passage from subalgebra intersections or conditional-expectation identities to meets of support projections is nontrivial and not justified. In particular, if the upgrading lemma is repaired by requiring commuting support projections, this lemma also fails to establish the needed commutativity. Therefore the boundary-cover input used in the final proof remains a major unproved technical assertion.

errors.title: Unsupported extension of an amenability central state to the relative small-at-infinity systems
errors.errored_block: Therefore $M$ has no amenable direct summand: if $pM$ were an amenable direct summand, Connes' amenability criterion would give an $M$-central state on $\B(L^2(pM))$, hence by extension an $M$-central state on every $S_{X_{M_{\Lk(v)}}}(M)$ normal on $M$, contradicting relative proper proximality.
errors.block_location: Proof of the theorem, second paragraph
errors.error_description: The proof asserts that an $M$-central state coming from an amenable direct summand $pM$ extends to an $M$-central state on each relative small-at-infinity operator system $S_{X_{M_{\Lk(v)}}}(M)$ that is normal on $M$. The reviewer notes that this extension is not constructed or justified. Passing from a central state on the corner algebra $\B(L^2(pM))$ to a state on the full relative boundary system with the required centrality and normality properties is a nontrivial step, so this paragraph does not establish the claimed absence of amenable direct summands.

secondary_issues.description: The proof does not clearly define or consistently distinguish the usual small-at-infinity operator system from the bidual small-at-infinity system and its support-projection model; this ambiguity underlies several of the projection-evaluation statements.

In Proposition \ref{prop:AFP}, the membership assertion $P_A,P_C\in S_{X_B}(M)$ is only sketched as a “direct Fock-space computation.” A reviewer regarded the strategy as correct but requested more details of the commutator calculation.
Some references to broad results, such as “Connes' amenability criterion,” are too vague to identify the precise theorem being invoked.

verdict_rationale: The proof is mathematically invalid. It relies on a false free-product criterion in the base case, and more fundamentally it uses an incorrect characterization/definition of proper proximality for tracial von Neumann algebras via a nonexistent “proper proximal ideal,” so the contradiction argument proves the wrong condition rather than proper proximality.

errors.title: False free-product criterion used for the base cases
errors.errored_block: We rely on the foundational dimension criteria for proper proximality of free products (Boutonnet, Ioana, and Peterson, 2021, Theorem 4.1): The free product of two tracial von Neumann algebras $A \ast B$ is properly proximal provided $\dim A \ge 2$ and $\dim B \ge 3$. By hypothesis, each vertex algebra $M_v$ possesses a trace-zero unitary, guaranteeing $\dim M_v \ge 2$.
errors.error_description: The proof invokes a claimed dimension-only criterion saying that $A\ast B$ is properly proximal whenever $\dim A\ge 2$ and $\dim B\ge 3$. The referees point out that this criterion is false as stated: proper proximality of such free products is not guaranteed merely by these dimension inequalities, and atom-size issues can produce, for instance, a one-dimensional summand under the stated assumptions. Consequently, the two $n=3$ base cases are not established by the argument given, so the induction has no valid base.

errors.title: Wrong characterization of proper proximality via a nonexistent ideal
errors.errored_block: By Boutonnet, Ioana, and Peterson (2021), a tracial von Neumann algebra $M$ is properly proximal if there does not exist an $M$-central state $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{B}(L^2M)$ extending the trace $\tau_M$ such that $\varphi(T) = 0$ for all operators $T \in \mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{prop}}(M)$, where $\mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{prop}}(M)$ is the norm-closed proper proximal ideal generated by $\{x e_D^M y \mid x, y \in M, D \subset M \text{ an amenable von Neumann subalgebra}\}$.
errors.error_description: This is not the definition or a valid criterion for proper proximality of tracial von Neumann algebras. The object called $\mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{prop}}(M)$, a “norm-closed proper proximal ideal” generated by the displayed basic-construction projections over amenable subalgebras, is not an existing ingredient in the correct definition, and the stated absence of a central state vanishing on it is unrelated to the actual notion. The subsequent contradiction argument assumes that failure of proper proximality yields such a state and then rules it out; since that equivalence is false, the proof establishes at most a different, hallucinated property and does not prove the theorem.

secondary_issues.description: The proof attributes both the free-product criterion and the von Neumann algebra definition of proper proximality to Boutonnet, Ioana, and Peterson (2021), but the cited theorem/reference does not contain these statements and predates the relevant general von Neumann algebra definition. The submission also has no bibliography.

Several referee comments identify non-mathematical presentation problems: excessive use of words such as “strictly,” “rigorously,” and “fatal,” unnecessary repetitions, and an unnecessary split into subcases in the construction of the shifts.
